The two waves that emerge from the slits interfere/superpose.

When their path difference is an integer multiple of the wavelength, a bright fringe is formed.

OR

When they reach the screen in phase, a bright fringe is formed.

4c

Brightness depends on the intensity of the incident light. 

Since intensity decreases with distance (it is inversely proportional to the square of the distance) and point C is farther away from the slits than point A, the fringe at point C will not be as bright as the fringe at point A.

question.html:
In an experiment, monochromatic light of wavelength 673 nm is incident on a double slit in vacuum. A screen is located at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits, where an interference pattern is formed. Bright fringes are observed at points A, B and C on the screen. The separation between point A and point C is 6 mm. 

a. Calculate the distance between the slits. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.

  [3]

b. Outline how bright fringes are formed on the screen.

  [2]

c. Explain why the fringe at point C is not as bright as the fringe at point A. 

  [2]

d. The vacuum between the slits and the screen is filled with oil. The wavelength of the monochromatic light in oil is 455 nm. 

i. Find the refractive index of oil.

  [1]

ii. State two changes to the bright fringes when the vacuum is filled with oil.

  [2]

e. In another experiment, light is incident on the boundary between oil and vacuum. When the angle of incidence is , the light wave travels along the boundary. Calculate .

  [2]
